clue.text: Way complete food is put together

parts.note: thorough means complete or utter
fare is food, as in simple fare

explanation.surface: A recipe tip: the way to put together a full meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road or public street is a way through for traffic.

clue.text: Loathe a person rabbiting on endlessly outside hospital

indicators.note: the trimmed word stands outside, wrapping round the hospital letter
endlessly means the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a bore is someone who talks tediously on and on; to rabbit on is British slang for chatter

explanation.surface: Disliking a chatterbox who won't stop talking near a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BORE to BOR, which goes 'outside' H to make BHOR after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to detest or hate intensely, a strong synonym.

clue.text: Traditional welcome from boxer in Cleveland, perhaps?

definitions.text: Traditional welcome from boxer in Cleveland, perhaps?

parts.words: Traditional welcome from boxer in Cleveland, perhaps?
parts.note: a boxer dog is a pet, and one riding in a car (Cleveland was once an American make of motor car) could be a car pet, here pictured as a red one

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fighter greeting fans in Ohio; the cryptic reading is a dog in a car. The answer is the strip laid out for honoured guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out a crimson strip of floor covering is the customary ceremonial greeting for VIPs.

clue.text: Fellow ambassador's instructions primarily about sticking together

parts.note: co- as a prefix means fellow, as in co-worker
HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador, plus the possessive S

indicators.note: primarily means only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A diplomat's orders are chiefly about unity among colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohesion is the state of holding or bonding together, as a unified group.

clue.text: Holiday accommodation a church first offered for hire

indicators.note: first says the church abbreviation comes before the letter A, though printed after it

parts.note: to let is to rent out, as in a room to let

explanation.surface: A church rents out its holiday cottage before anyone else does.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden Swiss-style cabin is a classic holiday lodging, as at ski resorts.

clue.text: Demote English supporter overcome by speed

indicators.note: overcome by puts the English supporter beneath, so inside, the word for speed

parts.note: rate means speed, as in at a rate of knots
a leg supports a body or a table

explanation.surface: An English fan is downgraded after being outrun.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate is to move down to a lower rank, as with football teams going down a division.

clue.text: Possibly Florentine workers' associations are able to

parts.note: TUs are trade unions, associations of workers
can means are able to

explanation.surface: Italian guilds of workers claim they are capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the capital of Tuscany, so a Florentine is one example of someone from that region.

clue.text: Impassive bloke carrying sale item from the East

indicators.note: carrying means the name holds the other piece within it

parts.note: Sid is a stock man's name, standing for any bloke

indicators.note: in an across clue, from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: a lot is an item put up at auction

explanation.surface: An unemotional man carries home an auction purchase from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' turns LOT into TOL, which SID is 'carrying': S-TOL-ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid describes someone calm and showing little emotion, unmoved.

clue.text: Half-hearted Liberal member going round posh gardens

indicators.note: going round means the outer pieces wrap round the inner ones

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
U means upper-class, posh
Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in west London

explanation.surface: An unenthusiastic Liberal politician strolls round smart botanic gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm, literally tepid, means lacking enthusiasm when used of support or feeling.

clue.text: Where jewels may be kept, to be on the safe side!

definitions.meaning: jewellery is stored inside a box or casket

definitions.text: to be on the safe side!
definitions.meaning: as a precaution, should something happen

explanation.definitionFit: One phrase both locates gems in a box and means as a precaution against a possibility.

clue.text: Happened to live like a strumpet, perhaps?

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a fallen woman is an old phrase for one who has lost her virtue

explanation.surface: A question about what became of someone living a disreputable life.
explanation.definitionFit: Befallen is the past participle of befall, to happen to someone.

clue.text: After drink, he'd pay recklessly for a seed capsule

indicators.note: after says the drink comes first, ahead of the shuffled letters

parts.note: pop is a fizzy soft drink

indicators.note: recklessly means the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Having had a drink, someone would pay over the odds for a seed pod.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried head of a poppy is the pod holding its seeds.

clue.text: Originally only composer to enjoy Tchaikovsky's work

indicators.note: originally means the starting letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A claim that only one composer could appreciate Tchaikovsky's music.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical piece for eight players or voices is a work of this kind.

clue.text: Novelist's German heritage misrepresented without it

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the novelist is the answer

indicators.note: misrepresented means the letters are shown in a false, scrambled form

explanation.surface: A writer's German roots are distorted by leaving something out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without it': take I and T out of GERMAN HERITAGE and rearrange the remaining twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Brighton Rock and The Power and the Glory was an English writer of fiction.

clue.text: Army medics in overturned desert vehicle

indicators.note: in places the medics inside the overturned word
in a down clue, overturned means the word is turned upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: to rat is to desert, as a rat leaves a sinking ship
RAMC is the Royal Army Medical Corps

explanation.surface: Military doctors are trapped in a desert vehicle that has rolled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' works in a down clue: the desert word is read upwards, giving TAR, which then takes the medics' initials inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramcar is a streetcar running on rails, a passenger vehicle.

clue.text: Work on the school map, perhaps: it's for examining pupils

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A geography lesson task, used to keep schoolchildren under examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges THE SCHOOL MAP into HTHALMOSCOPE. The pupils are not schoolchildren but the eye's.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye doctor uses this lighted instrument to look into the eye through the pupil.

clue.text: Bloomer Rumpole talked of in Albert Square?

indicators.note: Albert Square is where the BBC soap EastEnders is set, and its Cockney characters drop their aitches, so the name is pronounced as they would say it

parts.note: Horace Rumpole is the barrister hero of John Mortimer's Rumpole of the Bailey

explanation.surface: A gaffe by a TV barrister discussed in a soap's square.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Square is the East London setting of the TV soap EastEnders; a Cockney says Horace as 'Orris. 'Bloomer' is not a mistake here but a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is a kind of iris, a plant that flowers, so a playful bloomer.

clue.text: Received note about a bishop's method of execution

indicators.note: about means the received word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: got means received
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A bishop is told how he will be put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend) is a crossword convention for a bishop; the received word wraps round A plus that title, and the sol-fa note follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Garrotting, strangling with a cord or iron collar, was a form of capital punishment.

clue.text: Craze ultimately sure to decline

parts.note: a fad is a passing craze

indicators.note: ultimately means the closing letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A craze is bound to die out eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: To fade is to grow weaker or diminish gradually.

clue.text: Move round old poster originally hanging in inn

indicators.note: round means the word for move goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to rouse is to stir or move someone
an ad is an advertisement, a poster

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Instructions to relocate a vintage poster on a pub wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadhouse is a pub or inn on a main road, especially out of town.

clue.text: With support of large group in teacher's assembly, download course

indicators.note: in a down clue the download sits on top of, supported by, the pieces that follow

parts.note: an app is a downloaded program

indicators.note: in places the group inside the rearranged letters
assembly means the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: With a school's backing, a teacher's group downloads a course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges the teacher letters into ECHARTE, with the group put 'in' after ECHAR. 'With support of' places the download on top. The course is not a lesson but the pudding part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This baked fruit pudding is served as a dessert course.

clue.text: Victoria, perhaps, dispatching love drug

indicators.note: dispatching means getting rid of, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Victoria is a major London railway station
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A queen sending off a love potion.
explanation.definitionFit: A statin is a cholesterol-lowering medication.

clue.text: Denier's idle talk about popular English philosopher

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the denier is the answer

indicators.note: about means the talk wraps round the popular word

parts.note: gas is empty chatter
in means popular or fashionable
A. J. Ayer was an English philosopher of logical positivism

explanation.surface: A sceptic says the popular English thinker is all hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who contradicts or disputes a claim is a gainsayer.

clue.text: State of cat looking down on Catholic dignitary?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece looking down on another sits above it

parts.note: a queen is a female cat
Dom is a title given to some Catholic clergy, such as Benedictine monks

explanation.surface: A cat's haughty attitude towards a senior churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm ruled by a female monarch is a state or kingdom.

clue.text: Like insubstantial dress of agent welcoming Philby, perhaps

indicators.note: welcoming means the agent takes the name in

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
Kim Philby was the British double agent who spied for the Soviets

explanation.surface: A secret agent dressed scantily while receiving a notorious defector.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy clothing is scanty, using little material.

clue.text: Sea cow's sexual partner crossing an estuary at first

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the sea cow is the answer

indicators.note: crossing means the partner spans over the other piece, holding it

parts.note: a mate is a sexual partner, especially among animals

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A marine mammal's partner swims across a river mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: This large aquatic herbivore is commonly called a sea cow.

clue.text: Reportedly a person like Othello's affair

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: Othello was a Moor, a North African, so a person like him is a Moor

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's jealous general and his romance.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, often a secret one.

clue.text: Network originally selected to block border rising

indicators.note: to block means the letter sits inside, obstructing the other piece
in a down clue, rising means reading upwards

parts.note: a hem is the border of a cloth

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A selected net goes up to block the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns HEM into MEH, and S goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is a net or interlaced structure, a network.
